claims: A collapsed lung (pneumothorax) typically requires 1 to 2 weeks for initial healing of minor cases.
Full recovery from a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) sometimes takes 6 to 8 weeks depending on severity.
Small cases of a collapsed lung can resolve with rest in a few days.
More severe cases of a collapsed lung requiring chest tubes or surgery may take several weeks to a few months for complete recovery.
The lung typically re-inflates in 48 to 72 hours.
Small cases of a collapsed lung may only need rest and observation.
Larger collapses need chest tubes for 1–3 weeks.
Larger collapses may need surgery which may take longer.
Patients are often re-evaluated within two weeks to ensure the lung remains inflated.
Smoking severely increases the risk of recurrence of a collapsed lung and inhibits healing.
Changes in air pressure can trigger another collapse.
